title: The Unshakable Word and the Human Economy
english: Such a measuring line an angel holds in his hand to the prophet Zechariah, in order to measure how much the length and width of the true Jerusalem is. Furthermore, it is said: 'For indeed my inheritance is most strong for me,' (Ps 15:5) signifying through this that my inheritance truly becomes the most beautiful.

According to this, the signified 'strongest' is the God, whom Luke the evangelist writes about. Let no one consider the spoken word unsuitable for Christ (Ps 15:7). For if he needed an angelic measurement to show the human, what time would that be? If he was being wise regarding divinity from nature, being wise as God and source of wisdom, yet being wise as a man.

Since the following are said from the face of Christ (Ps 15:8), and the saying—the face from the Lord is my portion of inheritance (Ps 15:8)—is preserved without any change, whoever takes these verses spoken by the Lord does not sin. But those not having their thoughts about God properly ordered take them locally: that the Son is at the right hand of the Father because of 'Sitting at my right hands,' and that the Savior has sat after the ascension at the right hands of majesty, which is impossible to say. For if the Son is at the right hand of the Father locally, it is impossible for the Father to be at the right hand of the Son according to that same meaning; but the Son says: 'I saw the Lord at my right hand' (Ps 16:8). Therefore, it is not otherwise, according to place, to miss the Son at the right of the Father and the Father of the Son, just as 'I am in the Father and the Father in me' (John 10:30) is.

It must be observed, with the Savior understood as man and God, whether it is necessary to interpret these things according to the divinity or according to his economy according to the flesh. But it is not possible to piously take that the Word of God has spoken from the face of God the Father at his right hand and before himself, in such a way that he might remain unshakeable. For the God Word is unturning, nor is he existing by any amount of turning.

Since he denies the reason for the Word not being shaken, who is in the Father and at the right hand of the Father (for he is being in the Father and having him in himself, existing at the right hand and before him), the reason becomes that he who sees him and has him at the right hand is not shaken. Since therefore he denies this, it is rather impious to take these things regarding the only-begotten Son of God apart from his economy according to the flesh; it must be spoken harmoniously, he who has become truly human and humbled himself and became poor while being rich (2 Cor 8:9). For the human has become his, made like us in all things without sin; but his flesh was not without soul, as some wrongly thought. For how could flesh not having a soul say 'he has at the right hand a God and sees him always' so as not to sin? For a sinning movement arises from being shaken.

If these things are impossible (for the body does not see God, nor does it possess the thought of him who is at the right hand and before him), it remains, according to the economy, to speak these things humanly by the Word of God having become flesh truly, perfectly, and truthfully; for he will speak all things from one person, both the God-befitting and the human, as a man indeed has become, having the God at his right hand, he will not be shaken even if bitter things surround him, or if the kings of the earth stand against him and the rulers gather together against the Lord and against his Christ. For indeed, not having been shaken in soul, he did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth, having been tested in all things according to likeness without sin. Furthermore, it is brought forward how his heart rejoiced and his tongue exulted (Ps 34:10) over having the Lord at the right hand and before himself always. It is a praiseworthy exultation and gladness, he who does not become so because of chance things, but because of understanding.
